title: Integrated MF-C tool — macro-fiscal and climate
subtitle: built from the Global Fiscal Indicators dashboard (v1.3 panel, with the Climate Fiscal Risk Dashboard v1.5 series), the National Mitigation Investment Model (NMIM v0.2), the CDPM-based investment needs workbook (v1.1, cross-check) and MacroFiscalModels (GIMF / DIGNAD / DIGNAR-lite, LIC-DSF-lite; DIGNAD-R live).

readme_replace.What this is: The integrated macro-fiscal climate (MF-C) tool. It puts the Global Fiscal Indicators dashboard, the mitigation investment needs and the macro-fiscal models on one country page: what a country's net zero programme needs and costs, how much falls on the budget, how much carbon pricing can pay, and what it does to growth and debt - beside whether the country can pay for it, build it, and finance it. More modules will be added. The is_ccdr column flags the 98 economies with a published Country Climate and Development Report.
readme_replace.How it is organised: Sixteen blocks, in reading order. Four ASSESSMENT blocks carry the diagnosis: fiscal space, delivery, cost of capital, and financing. Three CONTEXT blocks explain it: fossil revenue in the budget, fossil trade and extraction, and power generation. Two INVESTMENT blocks give the need: Investment 1 (need by sector, incremental cost under three cost-of-capital lenses, the path to 2050) and Investment 2 (public investment needs: the budget need and who else pays); they read High / Medium / Low, like the Context blocks. Two MACRO blocks give the consequences: Macro 1 (how much of the budget need carbon pricing can pay) and Macro 2 (growth, debt, a cross-check with the other model family, debt-carrying capacity and debt risk); they carry no block verdict, because their rows point different ways. Five APPENDIX blocks are reference detail in grey: fuel pricing, power market regulation, macro-model inputs (including the debt-sustainability inputs), fiscal risk, and a cross-check of the investment need with the CDPM-based method. The Macro sheet has the GDP and debt paths with a live simple model; the DSA sheet has the debt-sustainability indicators against their thresholds.
readme_replace.Appendix C and D: Appendix C holds what the macro-fiscal models start from: WEO ratios, public investment (IMF ICSD, to 2019; used by the models), and the debt-sustainability inputs - external public debt and its share of all public debt (IDS; used by LIC-DSF-lite), the concessional share, CPIA, remittances and reserves (used for debt-carrying capacity) - with account ownership (Findex) as a candidate proxy for hand-to-mouth households (not yet used). The dashboard's Appendix D (the integrated scenario) is replaced here by the Macro 1 and Macro 2 blocks and the Macro and DSA sheets.
readme_replace.How to use it: Dashboard: pick a country in the yellow cell. Everything resolves - evaluation, score, value, observation year, coverage - grouped and coloured by block. Macro: the same country's GDP and debt paths - the integrated run, the other model family as a cross-check, and the live simple model - with charts; Macro_assumptions holds the simple model's yellow assumptions. DSA: the five LIC-DSF-lite indicators against their thresholds, before and with the programme. Data_wide is the cross-section, Data_long names the source file for every value, Scores holds the 1-10 rescaling, Spec is the indicator list, Sources lists the datasets.

readme_add: Investment 1 and 2 are MODEL OUTPUT, not data, from the National Mitigation Investment Model (InvestmentNeeds/national_model/, NMIM v0.2): 186 countries, 2024-2050, baseline and net zero, 2024 prices, built bottom-up from energy, power and emissions stocks. The same model feeds the macro-fiscal run in Appendix D. Values are % of NMIM's GDP for the year; the year column is the scenario year. See InvestmentNeeds/national_model/NMIM_Method_v0_2.md.

Incremental = net zero less the current-trends baseline. Incremental cost = annual capital charge on the incremental capital in service less fuel and operating savings (lens c also less local co-benefits); negative = net saving. Lens (a) uses the market WACC, (b) and (c) the World Bank 6% rate; the cost-of-capital penalty is (a) less (b), negative where market capital is cheaper than 6%.

NMIM splits all net zero investment by who repays it: P1 pure public (taxes), P2 regulated utility (tariffs), P3 contracted revenue (a public or regulated buyer), P4 viability gap (private with a public top-up), P5 pure private. Three public measures, narrow to wide: the direct budget need (P1 + the public 30% of P4: money the budget spends); plus regulated utilities (adds P2, a contingent liability where tariffs do not recover costs); and all investment needing public money or a public decision (P1 + P2 + all of P4). The PIMA-adjusted budget need divides the budget need by (1 - efficiency gap): the gap is mapped from PEFA PI-11 where the dashboard has it (40% at 1 to 13% at 4), else IMF (2015) income-group gaps (AE 13%, low income 40%, others 27%). Private capital is P3 + P5 + the other 70% of P4. The type shares are judgements applied to country data, not observed splits; power market structure rests on PSRT data that end in 2013.

Macro 1 and 2 are MODEL OUTPUT from the MacroFiscalModels integrated run, pre-computed in Python for 186 countries: dashboard -> NMIM (budget need) -> PriceFeasibility (feasible power-sector carbon pricing, revenue earmarked for the need) -> one macro model per country (GIMF-lite for most upper-middle and high-income countries, DIGNAD-lite for low-income and concessional borrowers, DIGNAR-lite where fossil rents are 10% of GDP or more) -> LIC-DSF-lite (low and lower-middle income only). The cross-check rows run the other model family on the same programme (DIGNAD-lite where GIMF-lite was chosen, GIMF-lite otherwise; GIMF-lite has no resource block). Debt-carrying capacity comes from the Composite Indicator where the dashboard has a CPIA score (IDA countries), medium otherwise; exports and imports are still assumptions. 'Today's path' is GDP with no trend growth from 2024; the baseline is the same model with no programme. Calibrations are illustrative.

The Macro sheet adds DIGNAD-R: DIGNAD-lite / DIGNAR-lite made recursive and written in formulas (MacroFiscalModels/ExcelDIGNAD), for the country picked on the Dashboard. Change the yellow cells on Macro_assumptions - disaster year, grant and concessional shares, pricing earmark, fiscal-rule speed - and it recalculates. It is DIGNAD-type for every country, has one fiscal instrument and no energy savings, so it differs from the integrated run, most for GIMF-lite countries and where the fiscal rule had to tighten.

Appendix E: fiscal risk from the World Bank Climate Fiscal Risk Dashboard v1.5 (ratings, rollover, external and short-term debt; climate in public investment management, budget tagging, a national climate fund). Appendix F: the same country's 2030 need from the CDPM-based global method (the v1.1 workbook: IHLEG and IEA-IFC group totals allocated to countries, with one public share per country group), as a cross-check on NMIM; the two will not match.
